topic: Why onions make you cry: tear gas from cut cells, eye nerves, chilling tip
caption:
That sting is not the smell. Cutting an onion breaks its cells and starts a chemical reaction. It makes a sulfur gas that reaches your eyes, so your tear glands flush it away.

Scientists only identified the enzyme behind it in 2002. Tip: a chilled onion can release less gas, and a sharp knife crushes fewer cells.

Send this to the friend who always cries over the cutting board. What is your own trick to stop onion tears?
